title: Fitting subscheme complement is the bounded-generator locus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. For $r\geq0$, let $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be the $r$-th Fitting ideal sheaf of $\mathcal F$: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ with $M=\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, a surjection $A^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow M$ and kernel $K$, it is the ideal generated by the $(n-r)\times(n-r)$ minors of the $(n-r)\times n$ matrices whose rows lie in $K$ (the unit ideal when $r\geq n$); these ideals do not depend on the surjection and commute with localization [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], so they glue. Let $Z_r\hookrightarrow S$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$. Then: (1) for every $S$-scheme $T$, the pullback $\mathcal F_T$ is locally generated by at most $r$ sections if and only if the structure morphism $T\to S$ factors through the open subscheme $S\setminus|Z_r|$; (2) for every $s\in S$ the following are equivalent: $s\notin|Z_r|$, i.e. $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)_s=\mathcal O_{S,s}$; $\mathcal F$ can be generated by at most $r$ sections on an open neighbourhood of $s$; the stalk $\mathcal F_s$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements as an $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-module.
